name: supply chain
owns: everything that arrives already written: registries, dependencies, build systems, CI runners, signing, third party scripts and tag managers
why_in_D: An application is mostly other people's code, and that code runs with the application's authority. No amount of application hardening helps when the dependency that renders the page is the thing that is malicious, or when the build pipeline can be made to ship different bytes than the repository contains.

factors.name: dependency resolution range
factors.def: whether the manifest allows a version range that can resolve to something new
factors.observable: a resolved version that is neither locked nor reviewed

factors.name: lockfile integrity enforcement
factors.def: whether the lock is verified on install or treated as advisory
factors.observable: an install that ignores the lock

factors.name: registry trust and namespacing
factors.def: whether the package namespace can be squatted or typosquatted
factors.observable: a similarly named package resolving as expected

factors.name: install time script execution
factors.def: whether a package can run code at install, before any review of its behaviour
factors.observable: a network request during install

factors.name: transitive dependency visibility
factors.def: whether the full dependency graph is known and reviewed or only the direct list
factors.observable: an unreviewed package present in the runtime tree

factors.name: dependency confusion across scopes
factors.def: whether an internal package name can be resolved from a public registry
factors.observable: a public package installed where an internal one was intended

factors.name: maintainer account takeover exposure
factors.def: whether a dependency is maintained by a single unprotected account
factors.observable: a release published without a second approver

factors.name: package signing verification
factors.def: whether signatures or provenance attestations are verified by the consumer
factors.observable: an unsigned package accepted

factors.name: release artefact provenance
factors.def: whether the published artefact can be rebuilt from the stated source
factors.observable: a rebuild that does not match the published bytes

factors.name: registry token scope
factors.def: whether a publishing token can also read private packages or modify others
factors.observable: a token with more authority than publishing needs

factors.name: vendor bundle composition
factors.def: what is actually inside a shipped vendor bundle, which is often more than the manifest says
factors.observable: a package in the bundle absent from the manifest

factors.name: third party script authority
factors.def: whether a third party tag can read the page, cookies and forms it is embedded in
factors.observable: a third party script reading values it has no need for

factors.name: tag manager injection surface
factors.def: whether a tag manager can add arbitrary script without a code change
factors.observable: new script execution introduced through configuration alone

factors.name: third party script integrity attribute
factors.def: whether subresource integrity or an equivalent pin is used
factors.observable: a changed third party file served without breaking the page

factors.name: CDN origin trust
factors.def: whether a CDN can serve arbitrary content under the site's origin
factors.observable: content served from the site that the site never authored

factors.name: JSONP and legacy script transport
factors.def: whether an endpoint serves executable script from data
factors.observable: a data endpoint executing as script

factors.name: analytics and support widget permissions
factors.def: what a widget can reach once it runs with page authority
factors.observable: a widget reading form values

factors.name: build cache poisoning
factors.def: whether a build cache entry can be supplied by an untrusted context
factors.observable: a build using an artefact that was not produced by the expected job

factors.name: CI runner privilege
factors.def: whether a job runs with credentials beyond the artefact it builds
factors.observable: a job able to push or deploy

factors.name: pull request triggered workflows
factors.def: whether a workflow runs code from an untrusted fork with secrets available
factors.observable: a secret present in a job triggered by an outsider

factors.name: workflow expression injection
factors.def: whether user controlled text is interpolated into a shell command
factors.observable: a command built from input such as a branch name

factors.name: secret exposure in logs
factors.def: whether output is masked and whether masking covers encoded forms
factors.observable: a secret in a log, masked or otherwise

factors.name: artefact signing coverage
factors.def: which artefacts are signed, and whether consumers check
factors.observable: an unsigned artefact consumed

factors.name: deployment credential lifetime
factors.def: whether deploy credentials are long lived and shared
factors.observable: a credential valid across environments and time

factors.name: git history leak
factors.def: whether secrets removed from code remain in history or in forks
factors.observable: a credential present in a historical commit

factors.name: repository visibility and forks
factors.def: whether a repository was ever public, and whether forks retain the content
factors.observable: content available from a fork after private

factors.name: git submodule and vendoring trust
factors.def: whether injected vendored code is reviewed as code or ignored as third party
factors.observable: a change to vendored code that nobody reviewed

factors.name: patch and update channel authentication
factors.def: whether update metadata is signed and whether the client verifies it
factors.observable: an update accepted from a mirror

factors.name: mirror and proxy substitution
factors.def: whether an install can be redirected to a mirror that serves different bytes
factors.observable: a package fetched from a non official index

factors.name: container base image freshness
factors.def: the age of the base image and whether it is rebuilt or pinned forever
factors.observable: known vulnerable packages in a fresh image

factors.name: image layer reproducibility
factors.def: whether an image can be rebuilt from its definition
factors.observable: two builds of the same definition differing

factors.name: dependency abandonment
factors.def: whether a dependency is unmaintained and therefore an unpatched hazard
factors.observable: no release or fix in a long window

factors.name: licence and legal exposure
factors.def: whether a dependency introduces an obligation the organisation is not meeting, which is a business risk with security consequences
factors.observable: a licence incompatible with the deployment model

factors.name: vulnerability disclosure reachability
factors.def: whether the project has a working disclosure path or ignores reports
factors.observable: an open report with no response

factors.name: advisory ingestion lag
factors.def: the delay between an advisory and an applied patch in this environment
factors.observable: a vulnerable version still deployed after the advisory date

factors.name: pinned version drift
factors.def: whether a pin hides an unfixed vulnerability because nobody revisits it
factors.observable: an old pinned version with a known issue

factors.name: generated code trust
factors.def: whether code generated by a tool or model enters the repo unreviewed
factors.observable: a generated file with unreviewed behaviour

factors.name: ide and editor extension authority
factors.def: what a developer's tooling can reach, which is the developer's whole environment
factors.observable: an extension reading repository content or secrets

factors.name: package manager config inheritance
factors.def: whether a repository level config can redirect or execute code on install
factors.observable: an install running a repository supplied command

factors.name: monorepo scope boundary
factors.def: whether one team's package can import another's internals and bypass its invariants
factors.observable: an import across a boundary that skips enforcement

factors.name: internal registry authentication
factors.def: whether the internal registry is reachable without credentials from inside the network
factors.observable: an internal package fetched anonymously

factors.name: backup of supply chain state
factors.def: whether the organisation can rebuild if a registry, CDN or repository disappears
factors.observable: a build failing when an upstream is unavailable

factors.name: model and dataset provenance
factors.def: where a model or fine tune came from and whether the source is verified
factors.observable: a model file with no verifiable origin

factors.name: model artefact deserialisation
factors.def: whether loading a model executes code, as pickle based formats do
factors.observable: code execution during model load

factors.name: prompt and tool definition supply
factors.def: whether prompts or tool schemas are fetched at runtime from a mutable source
factors.observable: behaviour change from a remote prompt edit

factors.name: agent tool registry trust
factors.def: whether an agent can be pointed at an unverified MCP server or tool endpoint
factors.observable: a tool from an unexpected server invoked

factors.name: plugin and extension marketplace review
factors.def: whether a plugin is reviewed before publication and after update
factors.observable: an update changing behaviour without review

factors.name: webhook subscription trust
factors.def: whether an outbound webhook target is validated, which is an SSRF and exfiltration path
factors.observable: a webhook delivered to an internal address

factors.name: email and dns provider delegation
factors.def: whether the sending domain can be spoofed or the DNS delegated to a weaker provider
factors.observable: a message passing authentication from an unauthorised sender

factors.name: ssl certificate automation trust
factors.def: whether the automation can be tricked into issuing for a name it should not
factors.observable: a certificate issued for an unintended name

factors.name: source map publication
factors.def: whether production source maps are public, exposing original code and comments
factors.observable: an original source file retrieved

factors.name: debug symbols and build metadata in release
factors.def: whether a release carries paths, usernames or commit identifiers
factors.observable: build metadata in a shipped artefact

factors.name: dependency count as attack surface
factors.def: the number of distinct packages whose compromise would reach this system
factors.observable: count of the resolved tree

factors.name: transitive install reach
factors.def: whether a package can pull another at install rather than at build, giving it later authority
factors.observable: a package installed at runtime

factors.name: reproducible build verification in ci
factors.def: whether CI checks that the artefact matches the source
factors.observable: a modified artefact passing the pipeline

factors.name: signed commit coverage
factors.def: whether commits and tags are signed and whether the policy is enforced
factors.observable: an unsigned commit merged

factors.name: branch protection completeness
factors.def: whether direct pushes, force pushes and unreviewed merges are prevented
factors.observable: a change landed without review

factors.name: release automation authority
factors.def: whether a release can be published by a job that never saw a human approval
factors.observable: a release produced with no approval step

factors.name: vendored binary trust
factors.def: whether a binary in the repo can be traced to a source and a build
factors.observable: a binary with no reproducible origin

factors.name: dependency update automation scope
factors.def: whether an automated update can merge itself, including a major version
factors.observable: an unreviewed major update merged

factors.name: package namespace ownership verification
factors.def: whether an organisation owns the exact names it depends on, including typos
factors.observable: an unclaimed lookalike name

factors.name: incident response for a compromised dependency
factors.def: whether the organisation can identify every system using a package within hours
factors.observable: time to enumerate exposure for a named package
